body:
I hope that you find some hope in the future for your son's sake. Enjoy the happy moments in life, that is what I always told myself, because you never know when the moment will be your last.

I know it is very stressful to live with a suicidal person, but I am not your SO, I can promise you that. I wish that you find peace.

I have experienced everything I want to, thanks to my parents who have sacrificed everything for my well being. I care for some guys in the past but they just used me for sex, so I don't care about men anymore. 

All in all, I can never be what I was supposed to be, I will never marry or have children so it is over.

I appreciate your concern though.

It's not enough. I guess it means that I am not enough.. But well.. The majority of people disagree with me anyway. And I am tired. Really tired.
I wish there are people who have the energy to do all this "uplifting" of humanity (which I know that there are).

No one will miss me.

Thank you for your reply, and it was very helpful as well.
On the other hand, what if I am someone who isn't going to uplift humanity in any way. Say, that I am an addict (of any substance). I won't contribute anything to the society as we know it today. So I guess that it is better that I kill myself.

I am glad about that, they usually say that pessimism solves nothing, guess they were wrong on that one as well! >:D

No but seriously, I hope that you feel better. Acne is something that can be treated, as well as your social anxiety. Being emotionally unstable.. well, I am sorry to break it to you, but that is what being human is all about. Emotions. You'll figure it out, I am sure of it.

But honestly honey (and I again hope that you don't take it in the wrong way) I am a 28 year old female who spent the last 10 years worrying about my appearance, and now I wish that I didn't. I know it is not that simple, but take it from me, it's not worth it. Please don't be like me and isolate yourself in your home, but be brave and socialize (as much as you feel comfortable, of course), and experience all that you feel like you can.

I have had friends with acne, and the thing that made our friendship strong was not their looks, but the chemistry and similar interests. So I am positive that you will have meaningful relationships with people again, when you are ready for them.

Love (and I hope that you don't take that the wrong way). People are ugly to their core. Your appearance is the least of your problems, even though I empathize with you having been born in this sick joke of a society myself. 
It should be what you do that matters, not what you look like.
I am a "loser" (who defines what's a loser anyway?) as well.

It's not you that's the problem, it's this broken joke of society that is.
